children: Australia's central bank will debate the case for a rate hike at its policy meeting this month, its deputy governor said on Tuesday, adding that inflation remained too high and risks were still skewed to the upside.
Andrew Hauser told the Australian Broadcasting Corporation he had become more worried about inflation after seeing the impact of data centres on his recent trip to the United States.
Hauser said the key question facing policymakers was if the three rate hikes so far this year were enough to tame inflation, or if more needed to be done.
The board will debate the case for a rate hike at the next meeting from September 28 to 29, he added.
"I could tell you today what I think I might want to do but there is nine people voting on it, so you'd be mad to take my advice," Hauser said when asked if a rate hike is "inevitable".

Markets now imply a 68% probability rates will rise by 25 basis points to 4.60% on September 29 after July inflation data surprised to the upside. There is also a 60% chance rates will reach 4.85% next year. (0#AUDIRPR)

Hauser said the central bank was not yet at the point where it needed to raise interest rates sharply to bring inflation to its 2%-3% target band, although a prolonged period of inflation overshooting targets could eventually require a stronger policy response.

"Inflation has been above target for a long period of time and at some point we will have to say that is long enough," he said. "We will raise interest rates further than otherwise we would need to do so - we are not at that point yet."
